UOS Beam Twin

A ray-traced digital twin of the University of Seoul campus. A gNB on the highest campus rooftop serves the area with 32 narrow beams. Click any point on the map to see which beam is best there, where simple geometry would point, and which beams the neural network asks the phone to measure.

Walking from the main gate to the IT Building

A 579 m walk along campus footpaths (3GPP BM-Case 2). At every 4 m step the phone measures only 4 beams, and a GRU that has seen the last four steps predicts the best beam for the next one. The chart shows its first guess. If the phone also checks the top-3 guesses (7 beams per step instead of 32), the mean loss on the test walks drops to 1.25 dB.

The live numbers at the top come from the same models retrained for this page with the same split and settings, so they can differ from the table by a few percentage points.

Digital twin

  • Buildings and terrain from OpenStreetMap and SRTM, converted to a Sionna RT scene.
  • gNB 3 m above the highest campus roof, 1×16 array, 32-beam DFT codebook from −60° to +60°.
  • Received power ray-traced for every beam on 4 m cells: about 29,000 locations.

Predictors

  • Position only: MLP with Fourier features of the (x, y, z) position.
  • Position + 4 measured: also gets 4 evenly spaced beams with 1 dB measurement error (3GPP BM-Case 1).
  • The phone measures the top-k predicted beams and keeps the strongest.

Fair evaluation

  • Campus split into 40 × 40 m blocks: 70 % train, 15 % validation, 15 % test.
  • Statistics use only test blocks, i.e. areas the model never saw (switch the map to “Train / test”).
  • Loss = power of the best beam minus power of the chosen beam, in dB.
